shorts.title: Reliability Beats Raw Talent
shorts.description: Homer explains why meaningful effort and being dependable can matter more than being the smartest person in the room.
shorts.socialCaption: You do not have to be the smartest person in the room to be the person everyone can count on.

shorts.title: Work Needs Humanity
shorts.description: A humane workplace does not require gimmicks. It requires work that people do not fantasize about crashing their car to avoid.
shorts.socialCaption: The point is not mandatory fun. The point is recognizing the humanity of the people doing the work.

shorts.title: Communication Is Not Always a Meeting
shorts.hook: The best communication is not always a meeting
shorts.description: Charlie connects military communications, technical support, and call-center leadership through the value of asynchronous visibility.
shorts.socialCaption: Sometimes the big picture appears when people can read the right conversation at the right time.

shorts.title: Leadership Is Environment Design
shorts.description: Leadership changes behavior by designing the environment around people, not merely by issuing more commands.
shorts.socialCaption: If you want behavior to change, inspect what the system rewards before writing another speech.

shorts.title: Simple Solutions Still Count
shorts.hook: The answer may be obvious to someone else
shorts.description: Simple answers often come from unexpected people. Good leaders make it safe for everyone to suggest them.
shorts.socialCaption: Listen broadly. The simplest useful answer may come from the person nobody thought to ask.

shorts.title: The Costa Rica Buffet Test
shorts.hook: He gamed the buffet without leaving his chair
shorts.description: Charlie tells the family story that revealed Homer's instinct to watch the whole system before acting.
shorts.socialCaption: Everyone else saw dinner. Homer saw the whole system and quietly found the easiest path through it.
